releases.body:
### Changed

- Releases are tagged automatically: every push to `main` reads the `package.json` version and, if
  it is not tagged yet, runs the release checks, then tags the commit `vX.Y.Z` and publishes from
  that tag ([Releasing](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#releasing)).
- New npm package description that more accurately represents what the plugin does.
- Bumped the dev dependencies `@opencode-ai/plugin` and `@opencode-ai/sdk` to 1.19.5, with
  `bun.lock` synchronized (dependency bumps only; no behavior change). The `@opencode-ai/plugin`
  peer range is unchanged.

### Fixed

- The TUI fits long commands by terminal columns, so CJK text and emoji no longer overflow the row
  or lose the end of the command, combining accents no longer cut it short, and a cut never splits
  a flag, an emoji or an accented letter ([#45](https://github.com/noppu-labs/opencode-permission-reviewer/issues/45)).

### Security

- GHSA-97r2-qh9m-474h, GHSA-wp97-x4hv-qvhp, GHSA-7rv5-mrxv-xcr9 and GHSA-9wx9-5pv9-3349 in
  `seroval` are documented as residual exposure, alongside GHSA-p6vx-979v-rg4c and
  GHSA-jp82-f5mq-hwhp. `seroval` arrives through `solid-js` 1.9.12, which `@opentui/solid` 0.7.0
  pins exactly. Only the SSR renderer `solid-js/web` imports it, and neither this plugin nor
  OpenTUI loads that renderer, so the vulnerable code is unreachable at runtime
  ([Supply chain](docs/SUPPLY-CHAIN.md#known-residual-exposure)). The upgrade is tracked in
  [#112](https://github.com/noppu-labs/opencode-permission-reviewer/issues/112).
- The audit no longer ignores GHSA-ch52-4w7c-c8xp (`http-cache-semantics`), which GitHub
  withdrew.

### Added

- Liquid AI (`liquid-ai/d1`, `liquid-ai/d1-ultra`) and Baseten
  (`baseten/decision-models/baseten-mammoth-27b-latest`,
  `baseten/decision-models/baseten-elephant-9b-latest`) System One reviewers, selected from one
  provider table. Keys come from `LIQUID_API_KEY` and `BASETEN_API_KEY`. A key that is not shaped
  like a Liquid AI key is never sent, and Liquid keys are redacted from reviewer evidence
  ([Reviewer models](docs/REVIEWER-MODELS.md#system-one-reviewers); ported from upstream 2.5.0).
- OpenRouter System One reviewers (`openrouter/<model>`, for example `openrouter/typesafe/jev-1.14`),
  keyed by `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. Listed models, routing suffixes such as `:free` and `:nitro`, and
  new `typesafe/jev-<n>` and `liquid/d1…` releases are accepted. Unbenchmarked models raise a
  config notice, and known-incompatible ones say every review will fail
  ([Reviewer models](docs/REVIEWER-MODELS.md#openrouter)).
- A weekly `openrouter-models` workflow that refreshes the list of OpenRouter decision models and
  opens a pull request against `develop`.
- Redaction of OpenRouter keys (`sk-or-v1-…`) in reviewer evidence.

### Changed

- User-facing text says "System One" instead of "Jev" when it describes the mechanism: attribution
  lines, toasts, config warnings and the docs. "Jev" now names only the Jev model itself.
- The minimum Bun is now 1.3.14 (was 1.3.0), the floor `@opentui/core` 0.7 declares. The TUI
  dependencies move from `@opentui/core` and `@opentui/solid` 0.5.11 to 0.7.0, which
  `@opencode/plugin` 2.2.0 pins exactly.
- Update the `@opencode/client` dependency to 2.2.0, from upstream. OpenCode 2.2.0 joins the
  real-host matrix as a verified V2 host.
- Development tooling updates (Biome 2.6, knip, tsdown, `@types/bun`) with no behaviour change.
  The development tree also clears new `zod` and `undici` advisories.

### Fixed

- On OpenCode V2, a reviewer model that lacks the default `medium` variant now runs with its own
  default variant instead of escalating every request, including when `medium` is set explicitly.
  Any other variant the model lacks still fails closed, and the error lists the variants the model
  offers (ported from upstream 2.5.0).
- OpenCode session IDs (`ses_…`) under a session key are kept in reviewer evidence instead of being
  redacted as credentials. Lookalike values, and session IDs under other keys, are still redacted
  (ported from upstream 2.5.0).
- Package-script evidence now starts from the shell tool's `workdir`, so `bun run x` in a
  workspace package reports that package's script, not the root one. A workdir that is invalid or
  does not exist is reported as unresolved, and the read roots do not widen (ported from upstream
  2.5.0).

### Security

- `@opentui/solid` 0.7.0 pins `@babel/core` 7.29.7, so consumer installs no longer carry
  GHSA-4x5r-pxfx-6jf8 (`@babel/core <= 7.29.0`).

### Changed

- The README's install section leads with `opencode plugin add` on OpenCode V2 and keeps the
  `bunx ... init --tui` command for V1, where `opencode plugin` does not register the TUI
  overlay. The README also opens with a banner image.
- The npm package has a fuller description and more search keywords.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `MIGRATION.md`, `NOTICE` and
  `LICENSE-APACHE` moved from the repository root to `docs/`. The npm package now ships
  `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `docs/NOTICE`, `docs/LICENSE-APACHE` and `docs/SECURITY.md` in place of
  the root copies.
- No behaviour change: the plugin code, package exports, command-line interface and
  configuration are the same as in 3.2.2.

### Changed

- Internal follow-ups to the `src/` restructure: one shared logger type, clearer names for the
  context reader and the review audit-record helpers, and a stricter layer test. No behaviour
  change: the package exports, command-line interface, configuration and shipped files are the
  same as in 3.2.1.

### Changed

- Internal restructure of `src/` into layered modules, adapters and helpers, with a test that
  enforces the dependency direction. No behaviour change: the package exports, command-line
  interface, configuration and shipped files are the same as in 3.2.0.
